newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher despite profit-taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Wednesday despite some profit-taking, with traders saying the market had stabilized at current levels.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.24 percent, or 0.50 points, to 211.53 on all-share turnover of 87 million shekels against 100 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.23 percent to 219.86.
"The market looks like a runner who is getting close to the finish-line and is losing his breath," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
"The year will end soon and the market is tired. The mutual funds know that they will show positive returns and now they can rest," he added.
Traders said the market is stabilizing at current levels as investors await fresh news and further profit-taking.
"Investors want to see the budget approval and a rate cut," the Hapoalim trader said.

"The market made a very nice move during the last two months and now its time for a correction. Its only natural that investors are taking profits, which this is a necessary step before the market continues to rise," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities.
Elbit Ltd fell 3.0 percent to 2,263 after its Nasdaq-traded share dropped 5.6 percent on Tuesday.
Shekem surged 9.5 percent to 103, which traders said was only a technical correction after the sharp drop in its share price over the last few months.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 2.0 percent to 29,212 on volume of 6.1 million shekels; Israel Land Development Co, which gained 0.25 percent to 1,059 on turnover of 4.6 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 2.0 percent to 151,363 on volume of 2.9 million shekels.
